naive_async.execution: Version-unaware reward normalization with a two-group delayed buffer: generate g0 (v0/v1 transition) and g1 under policy 0; train g1; generate g2 under policy 1 while g0 remains queued; then train stale g0, g2 and g3. Policy and verifier lag limits both equal 1 for the naive negative control; g4 is unused.
naive_async.expected_invalid_updates: outcome measured by independent v1 recomputation

sync.execution: Synchronous collection and delivery under v1; groups 0..4 use successive policy versions and group 4 is unused after four commits.

vare_async.execution: The same producer schedule, with authenticated VARE admission. The trajectory store holds old-policy g0 beside current-policy g2; it quarantines all of g0, trains g2 during the bounded two-group scan, then trains g1,g3,g4 for four total updates. In no_drift, g0 is label-correct but policy-stale, measuring the valid-data rejection cost.

crash_recovery.condition: Run only after the full v7 primary run and its independent audit pass, including a passed false_accept pilot gate. No crash run is inferred from the earlier single-update v6 result.
crash_recovery.failure_action: Stop at the first failed kill or state mismatch; preserve all cases and do not rerun the same cutpoint.
crash_recovery.harness_seed_role: Fixed legacy crash-harness replay-order/run identifier only; all model weights and the target group come from the fresh v7 seed. No crash worker samples a new rollout.
crash_recovery.source: The false_accept/vare_async arm from this v7 run. Rebase the exact checkpoint after its first two committed updates as local policy-0, then use its retained g-03 rollout and third-update checkpoint as the reference continuation.

hardware.host: Apple M1 Pro, 32 GB unified memory

hypothesis: Under matched model, rollout, and verifier-call budgets, mixed-version reward groups can change real repeated GRPO updates. The VARE authenticated trajectory path should quarantine groups spanning a verifier transition and retain useful fresh updates, while a version-unaware asynchronous negative control can commit an update trained on labels inconsistent with the current independent oracle.
limits: One model, synthetic task semantics, one fixed model seed per verifier scenario and one host.
Scenario selection tests distinct failure modes; it does not estimate their prevalence in natural verifiers.
CPU model generation is serialized. The bounded delayed queue tests version consistency and queue residence, not parallel throughput speedup.
The async stale group is simultaneously one policy version behind and verifier-stale; the no-drift control isolates policy-only staleness and quantifies valid-data rejection.
The optional five-cut crash extension reuses one retained third-update group across fault cutpoints to control recovery inputs; those cutpoints are not independent quality replications.
A green mechanism run is not evidence of coding-task capability or general RL robustness.

continue_only_if: pilot naive g0 has at least one label disagreement under the independently recomputed v1 oracle
pilot naive g0 rewards are nonconstant and the prespecified naive g1 update commits
the buffered async queue is independently evidenced with policy versions 0 and 1 and, in drift scenarios, verifier versions 0 and 1
VARE quarantines every g0 member and consumes fresh buffered g2 exactly once
VARE commits exactly four actual optimizer updates and every committed group has nonconstant advantages
pilot_gate.failure_action: Stop without resampling or altering the task, verifier, prompt, seed, or policy schedule; preserve the partial pilot and report NO-GO.

primary_metric: Per drift scenario, invalid committed optimizer updates among four, naive_async versus vare_async, where invalid means at least one training-group reward differs from an independent recomputation under authoritative v1. The no-drift condition separately measures VARE rejection of label-correct but policy-stale g0.

protocol_amendment.change: Read training and evaluation prompts from workload, validate the complete protocol shape before model construction, and use the nested seed consistently. No task semantics, task order, budgets, arm schedule, scoring, thresholds, or analysis changed.
protocol_amendment.reason: The v7.2 invocation constructed and checkpointed the initial TinyStories policy, then failed when the runner requested heldout_prompts at the protocol top level; evaluation prompts are nested under workload.evaluation.prompts.

resource_limits.abort: Stop at first source/model identity mismatch, nonidentical matched initial g0 rollout, incomplete/degenerate training group, non-finite replay, optimizer replay error >=2e-6, behavior-logprob error >=1e-4, unexpected optimizer/promotion count, stale group admitted by VARE, per-arm or total wall cap at a group boundary, 8 GiB peak RSS, or 256 MiB positive swap growth. Preserve partial output; no replacement runs.

scope: A bounded synthetic reward-systems study using real TinyStories-1M sampling and actual RVL AdamW/GRPO updates on one CPU host. It includes a deliberately delayed two-group queue spanning behavior-policy versions and verifier versions, followed conditionally by five process-kill recoveries of a third sequential update. It does not measure coding-agent capability, natural verifier-drift prevalence, or parallel asynchronous speedup.

statistical_plan.independent_unit: The three deliberately distinct verifier semantic changes; no rollout member or repeated optimizer update is treated as an independent unit.
statistical_plan.primary_comparison: Report paired per-scenario differences in invalid committed updates and a descriptive one-sided exact sign-test resolution across three purposive drift semantics. If all three differences favor VARE, the smallest nominal p under an independent-sign assumption is 0.125. This is not population-level evidence or a confirmatory superiority claim.
statistical_plan.quality_claim_rule: If all held-out scores across incumbent and updated policies are constant, report only consistency/recovery mechanics and no policy-quality claim. Synthetic held-out scores never imply coding capability.
statistical_plan.sample_size: Three drift scenarios plus one no-drift control; one fixed seed per scenario.
statistical_plan.secondary_metrics: Report denominators and raw scenario results for false accepts/rejects, reward-ranking inversions, valid stale trajectories rejected, queue depth and group residence, policy/verifier lag, held-out changes, CPU/wall time, checkpoint I/O, RSS and swap. No confirmatory p-values for secondary metrics.

workload.description: Each arm samples 5 groups of 8 completions and makes 4 optimizer commits. Sync samples/delivers groups 0..4 sequentially and trains on 0..3. Async samples g0 and g1 under policy 0, trains g1, samples g2 under policy 1 while g0 remains buffered, then delivers g0 before g2. Naive trains on g1,g0,g2,g3; VARE quarantines g0, consumes the buffered g2 during the stale-group scan, then trains g3,g4. Group 4 is the matched unused group for sync/naive. Every sampled group receives 8 verifier calls.
